title: When the Lights Went Out in Venezuela

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson, and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档关于设计之爱及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you, and you turned a DJ booth
sentences.zh: 即便是在黑胶唱片时代的夜店当DJ，你每晚也要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去工作，然后你把DJ台

sentences.en: into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 变成了一个活生生的、临时搭建的精美50年历史文物博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: An economic collapse, a crumbling infrastructure, a contested presidential election.
sentences.zh: 经济崩溃、基础设施瓦解、总统大选争议不断。

sentences.en: Venezuela was already in crisis.
sentences.zh: 委内瑞拉本已陷入危机。

sentences.en: Then the power went out.
sentences.zh: 接着，停电了。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, April 10th.
sentences.zh: 今天是4月10日，星期三。

sentences.en: Nick, tell me the story that you were told about what happened in Venezuela last month.
sentences.zh: 尼克，跟我讲讲你听到的关于上个月委内瑞拉发生的事情。

sentences.en: So it was a Thursday last month in Maracaibo.
sentences.zh: 那是上个月的一个周四，在马拉开波。

sentences.en: And David Ardila, who's a publicist there,
sentences.zh: 大卫·阿迪拉，当地的一位公关人员，

sentences.en: was sitting at his desk when the lights went out.
sentences.zh: 当时正坐在办公桌前，灯突然灭了。

sentences.en: Nick Casey covers Latin America for The Times.
sentences.zh: 尼克·凯西为《纽约时报》报道拉美新闻。

sentences.en: This wasn't anything that surprised him because the lights were always going out in the city.
sentences.zh: 这并没有让他感到惊讶，因为城里总是停电。

sentences.en: This is a place on the edge of the electric grid in Venezuela.
sentences.zh: 这里位于委内瑞拉电网的边缘地带。

sentences.en: So it was not unusual for the lights to go out for a number of hours.
sentences.zh: 所以停电几个小时并不是什么稀奇事。

sentences.en: There were rolling blackouts there.
sentences.zh: 那里经常有轮流停电。

sentences.en: Usually by 4 p.m., the lights are back on.
sentences.zh: 通常下午4点前电就回来了。

sentences.en: But then he got a call from his wife who said
sentences.zh: 但后来他接到妻子的电话，说

sentences.en: there was not just a power outage in Maracaibo, but all over Venezuela.
sentences.zh: 不仅是马拉开波，整个委内瑞拉都停电了。

sentences.en: This was something that wasn't usual.
sentences.zh: 这就不寻常了。

sentences.en: This was something no one had really seen or remembered before.
sentences.zh: 这是大家从未见过或经历过的事情。

sentences.en: We're talking about a country of 30 million people and almost no one has electricity.
sentences.zh: 我们说的是一个拥有3000万人口的国家，几乎所有人都没有电。

sentences.en: So the power is out across Venezuela.
sentences.zh: 所以整个委内瑞拉都停电了。

sentences.en: Across the entire country.
sentences.zh: 全国范围的停电。

sentences.en: And that means things get very ugly very faSt.
sentences.zh: 这意味着局势很快就会变得非常糟糕。

sentences.en: What had happened to trigger this blackout?
sentences.zh: 是什么引发了这次停电？

sentences.en: According to the electricians' union, it was a brush fire that took place over some cables that were feeding the country.
sentences.zh: 据电工工会称，是一场灌木丛火灾烧毁了为全国供电的电缆。

sentences.en: But you have to ask yourself, if one fire is able to turn off all the power to a country, there must be a bigger problem there.
sentences.zh: 但你不得不问自己，如果一场火灾就能让全国断电，那说明那里一定存在更大的问题。

sentences.en: And the problem is that Venezuela is in the middle of an economic collapse.
sentences.zh: 问题在于委内瑞拉正处于经济崩溃之中。

sentences.en: That means that key infrastructure in the country isn't getting built and what's there isn't getting repaired.
sentences.zh: 这意味着国家的关键基础设施得不到建设，现有的也得不到维修。

sentences.en: On top of this, there's massive political unreSt.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，还有大规模的政治动荡。

sentences.en: Juan Guaido, the country's self-proclaimed leader, is calling for his supporters to take to the streets again to step up pressure on President Nicolas Maduro
sentences.zh: 该国自封的领导人胡安·瓜伊多呼吁支持者再次走上街头，加大对尼古拉斯·马杜罗总统的压力，

sentences.en: and demand new elections.
sentences.zh: 并要求举行新的选举。

sentences.en: Maduro has also called on his supporters to rally today.
sentences.zh: 马杜罗也呼吁他的支持者今天集会。

sentences.en: The power struggle between Guaido and Maduro has brought the country to a standstill.
sentences.zh: 瓜伊多和马杜罗之间的权力斗争让国家陷入了停滞。

sentences.en: And that as a huge electricity...
sentences.zh: 而这造成了巨大的电力……

sentences.en: There are still two men who say that they're the president of Venezuela and Guaido actually has the support of America and 50 other countries as well.
sentences.zh: 现在仍有两个人声称自己是委内瑞拉总统，而瓜伊多实际上得到了美国和其他50个国家的支持。

sentences.en: This is extremely unresolved.
sentences.zh: 这极其悬而未决。

sentences.en: Donald Trump is saying that Maduro needs to step down and let Guaido be the president.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普表示，马杜罗需要下台，让瓜伊多担任总统。

sentences.en: So in this moment, when the power goes out to 30 million Venezuelans, it's not entirely clear who runs the country or who will be solving the blackout.
sentences.zh: 所以此刻，当3000万委内瑞拉人断电时，谁在治理国家，或者谁来解决停电问题，并不完全清楚。

sentences.en: Not at all.
sentences.zh: 一点也不清楚。

sentences.en: And it's becoming clear to everybody that Maduro can't do even the most basic thing that a government should be doing, which is keeping the lights on.
sentences.zh: 而且大家越来越清楚，马杜罗连政府最基本的工作——维持供电——都做不到。

sentences.en: So these two events aren't directly connected to each other, but you suddenly see that one is starting to feed off of the other, which is this discontent that brought Guaido
sentences.zh: 所以这两件事虽然没有直接联系，但你突然发现一件事开始加剧另一件事，即导致瓜伊多

sentences.en: to the forefront in Venezuelan politics is now being doubled by the fact that Maduro can't provide electricity.
sentences.zh: 走上委内瑞拉政治前台的不满情绪，现在因为马杜罗无法提供电力而加倍了。

sentences.en: It's underscoring this question which everybody has asked in Venezuela, which is, if you can't provide power, are you actually providing a state?
sentences.zh: 这凸显了委内瑞拉每个人都在问的问题：如果你连电都供不上，你还能算是一个政府吗？

sentences.en: So I decided to go to Maracaibo, which is Venezuela's second largest city.
sentences.zh: 所以我决定去委内瑞拉第二大城市马拉开波。

sentences.en: It's also at the end of the electric grid.
sentences.zh: 它也处于电网的末端。

sentences.en: So we knew that this was going to be a place where there was going to be problems, and the problems were going to be very big.
sentences.zh: 所以我们知道这里会出问题，而且问题会非常严重。

sentences.en: So you can hear the sound of the generator here, which is out of a small truck, and there's basically a line of phones where everybody has plugged in.
sentences.zh: 你可以听到这里发电机的声音，它来自一辆小卡车，那里基本上排着一长队手机，每个人都在充电。

sentences.en: You have to remember that Maracaibo sits on the Caribbean coaSt.
sentences.zh: 你必须记住，马拉开波位于加勒比海岸。

sentences.en: It's a really hot, sweltering city.
sentences.zh: 那是一个非常炎热、闷热的城市。

sentences.en: The old joke in Maracaibo was that it's the coldest city in Venezuela because everybody has air conditioning.
sentences.zh: 马拉开波的老笑话是，它是委内瑞拉最冷的城市，因为每个人都有空调。

sentences.en: But now there was no air conditioning.
sentences.zh: 但现在没有空调了。

sentences.en: And after a few days, things started to come apart.
sentences.zh: 几天之后，一切开始分崩离析。

sentences.en: People were running out of food.
sentences.zh: 人们的食物快吃完了。

sentences.en: And it started with the looting.
sentences.zh: 骚乱从抢劫开始。

sentences.en: There were big crowds of more than 1,000 people that suddenly gathered looking for food.
sentences.zh: 突然聚集了超过1000人的大群人，在寻找食物。

sentences.en: When these crowds first went to the grocery stores, they sacked almost every single supermarket that was in Maracaibo.
sentences.zh: 当这些人第一次冲进杂货店时，他们洗劫了马拉开波几乎所有的超市。

sentences.en: But then they kept going.
sentences.zh: 但他们没有停下来。

sentences.en: They started taking anything that was available.
sentences.zh: 他们开始拿走任何能拿到的东西。

sentences.en: People were suddenly taking furniture.
sentences.zh: 人们突然开始搬走家具。

sentences.en: They were taking washers and dryers.
sentences.zh: 他们搬走了洗衣机和烘干机。

sentences.en: They were taking all of these appliances and anything that they could.
sentences.zh: 他们拿走了所有这些电器以及任何他们能拿的东西。

sentences.en: After this massive economic crisis, you can suddenly imagine if you could get your hands on something that was of value and worth a lot, you would go for it.
sentences.zh: 在经历了这场巨大的经济危机后，你可以想象，如果你能弄到有价值且值钱的东西，你肯定会去抢。

sentences.en: You would take it.
sentences.zh: 你会拿走它。

sentences.en: Especially if there's no state.
sentences.zh: 尤其是在没有政府的情况下。

sentences.en: There's no one patrolling.
sentences.zh: 没有人巡逻。

sentences.en: There's no one patrolling?
sentences.zh: 没有人巡逻？

sentences.en: No one.
sentences.zh: 一个人都没有。

sentences.en: I talked to many store owners who said that they were waiting for the police to come, and the police didn't come.
sentences.zh: 我采访了许多店主，他们说他们一直在等警察来，但警察没来。

sentences.en: Part of the reason for that is because the police themselves, their paychecks are worthless.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是警察自己的工资也一文不值。

sentences.en: People aren't showing up to the jobs.
sentences.zh: 人们不再去上班了。

sentences.en: Things are just coming apart this way.
sentences.zh: 事情就是这样分崩离析的。

sentences.en: What's your name again?
sentences.zh: 你叫什么名字来着？

sentences.en: Marbella Jiménez.
sentences.zh: 玛贝拉·希门尼斯。

sentences.en: Marbella.
sentences.zh: 玛贝拉。

sentences.en: I talked to one woman who was selling vegetables out in front of one of the places that got completely torn apart.
sentences.zh: 我采访了一位妇女，她在一家被彻底摧毁的店面前卖蔬菜。

sentences.en: People were setting fire to the stores.
sentences.zh: 人们在放火烧店。

sentences.en: And I asked her why they were setting fire, and she said...
sentences.zh: 我问她为什么要放火，她说……

sentences.en: It wasn't actually out of spite.
sentences.zh: 其实并不是出于恶意。

sentences.en: It was because it was dark, and they couldn't see inside the store.
sentences.zh: 是因为天太黑了，他们看不见店里的东西。

sentences.en: Burn the store in order to see what you are stealing.
sentences.zh: 烧掉商店才能看清你在偷什么。

sentences.en: Burn the store, take as much as you can, and leave it to be burned to the ground.
sentences.zh: 烧掉商店，尽可能多地拿走东西，然后任由它烧成灰烬。

sentences.en: And that's what we saw by the time we were there.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们到达时所看到的情景。

sentences.en: A lot of these places were just in embers at that point.
sentences.zh: 当时很多地方只剩下余烬。

sentences.en: There were so few places that were remaining, so few pharmacies that were even remaining.
sentences.zh: 剩下的地方太少了，剩下的药店也寥寥无几。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I ran into one man who had tongue cancer.
sentences.zh: 我遇到了一个患有舌癌的男人。

sentences.en: He was a professor.
sentences.zh: 他是一位教授。

sentences.en: And at that point, you could see his face was completely bulging in tumors that were taking over the sides of his chin, below his jaw, affecting how he could speak.
sentences.zh: 当时你可以看到他的脸完全肿胀，肿瘤长满了下巴两侧，一直延伸到下颌下方，影响了他的说话能力。

sentences.en: He hadn't been treated for weeks,
sentences.zh: 他已经几周没有接受治疗了，

sentences.en: and he told me that he didn't think he had any hope of being able to find medication at that point.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我，他觉得现在已经没有任何希望找到药物了。

sentences.en: Because there's nowhere that was going to be able to sell it to him.
sentences.zh: 因为根本没有地方能卖给他。

sentences.en: There was so much looting that seemed to be taking place simultaneously across Maracaibo.
sentences.zh: 马拉开波各地似乎同时发生了大量的抢劫。

sentences.en: And then there were firefights that were breaking out between the looters and the owners as people were trying to break into stores.
sentences.zh: 当人们试图闯入商店时，抢劫者和店主之间爆发了枪战。

sentences.en: Firefights and then there's gunfire.
sentences.zh: 枪战，到处都是枪声。

sentences.en: Gunfire.
sentences.zh: 枪声。

sentences.en: This was just a total anarchy in parts of Maracaibo.
sentences.zh: 马拉开波的部分地区完全陷入了无政府状态。

sentences.en: Now these people started to end up in the hospitals.
sentences.zh: 现在这些人开始涌入医院。

sentences.en: They're going to hospitals at that point that didn't have any electricity.
sentences.zh: 他们去的是当时没有任何电力的医院。

sentences.en: So how are you going to take care of people with gunshot wounds when there's no electricity?
sentences.zh: 那么在没有电的情况下，你要怎么照顾枪伤患者呢？

sentences.en: I needed to see what was going on.
sentences.zh: 我需要看看发生了什么。

sentences.en: But you can't get into hospitals in Venezuela if you're a journaliSt.
sentences.zh: 但如果你是记者，你就进不去委内瑞拉的医院。

sentences.en: Many of them are militarized.
sentences.zh: 其中许多医院已被军事化。

sentences.en: People have been arrested for going into these hospitals.
sentences.zh: 有人因为进入这些医院而被捕。

sentences.en: They don't want you to see.
sentences.zh: 他们不想让你看到。

sentences.en: This is really at the core of what Maduro can't do in this country.
sentences.zh: 这确实是马杜罗在这个国家无法解决问题的核心。

sentences.en: This is very sensitive to the government.
sentences.zh: 这对政府来说非常敏感。

sentences.en: They can't treat people.
sentences.zh: 他们无法救治病人。

sentences.en: So this has even put the hospital staff and the doctors under threat.
sentences.zh: 所以这甚至让医院的工作人员和医生也受到了威胁。

sentences.en: They're afraid to speak.
sentences.zh: 他们不敢说话。

sentences.en: But I was able to find a couple of doctors who were able to talk to me behind closed doors in another facility.
sentences.zh: 但我还是在另一家机构找到了几位愿意在闭门情况下与我交谈的医生。

sentences.en: And here we're actually going to change the voices of these doctors so that their identities are protected and they don't get in trouble for talking to you.
sentences.zh: 在这里，我们实际上会改变这些医生的声音，以保护他们的身份，让他们不会因为和你交谈而惹上麻烦。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And these doctors were telling me when I met them that this had been a place where it was already almost impossible to treat patients.
sentences.zh: 当我见到这些医生时，他们告诉我，这里本来就已经几乎无法救治病人了。

sentences.en: There was very little water.
sentences.zh: 水非常少。

sentences.en: They were having to wash their hands using bottled water.
sentences.zh: 他们不得不使用瓶装水来洗手。

sentences.en: They were running out of soap.
sentences.zh: 肥皂也快用完了。

sentences.en: They didn't have medicines that they needed.
sentences.zh: 他们没有所需的药物。

sentences.en: And then suddenly they didn't have any electricity.
sentences.zh: 然后突然间，他们连电都没有了。

sentences.en: One of the doctors I talked to said the first thing that hit you was the smell.
sentences.zh: 我采访的一位医生说，首先冲击你的是气味。

sentences.en: There is a stench that is horrific there.
sentences.zh: 那里有一种可怕的恶臭。

sentences.en: And as the people were coming in with injuries from these lootings that were taking place, gunshot wounds, glass wounds because they had broken down one of the windows,
sentences.zh: 当人们带着抢劫中受的伤进来时，有枪伤的，有因为砸碎窗户而受的玻璃割伤，

sentences.en: doctors didn't know how to treat them initially.
sentences.zh: 医生起初不知道该怎么处理。

sentences.en: They were trying to treat them.
sentences.zh: 他们正在尽力救治。

sentences.en: And in some cases, according to one of the medical officials I talked to, people were getting amputations that they didn't necessarily need because this was the only way
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，据我采访的一位医疗官员说，人们接受了本不必要的截肢手术，因为这是唯一的方法，

sentences.en: that they were going to save this person was doing an amputation when ordinarily if you had had everything that you needed, you would have been able to do something else
sentences.zh: 只有通过截肢才能救下这个人，而通常如果你拥有所需的一切，你本可以做点别的，

sentences.en: for this person besides take off their arm or their leg.
sentences.zh: 而不是切掉他们的手臂或腿。

sentences.en: this placard is literally costing people their limbs.
sentences.zh: 这场停电真的让人们付出了肢体的代价。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And on top of that, even in the morgue there's no power.
sentences.zh: 最糟糕的是，连太平间都没有电。

sentences.en: The morgue was abandoned,
sentences.zh: 太平间被废弃了，

sentences.en: contaminated, full of moscas, of insects,
sentences.zh: 受到污染，到处都是苍蝇和昆虫，

sentences.en: so the bodies are starting to rot there.
sentences.zh: 所以尸体开始在那里腐烂。

sentences.en: That's during the day, but then the night starts to hit and you have to continue doing work as people are coming in to try to get treated.
sentences.zh: 那是白天的情况，但到了晚上，你必须继续工作，因为人们还在不断涌入寻求救治。

sentences.en: People were pulling out their cell phones to use the light by their cell phones to try to treat people at that point.
sentences.zh: 当时人们掏出手机，用手机的光来尝试救治病人。

sentences.en: This doctor told me that you could hear people screaming.
sentences.zh: 这位医生告诉我，你能听到人们的尖叫声。

sentences.en: But you couldn't tell where the screams were necessarily coming from because the whole place was dark.
sentences.zh: 但你无法判断尖叫声到底来自哪里，因为整个地方一片漆黑。

sentences.en: At a certain point, a couple of days into this, there was a robbery when an armed group came in and went to the third floor of one of the hospitals and started to steal
sentences.zh: 在停电几天后的某个时刻，发生了一起抢劫案，一个武装团体闯入医院三楼，开始抢劫

sentences.en: from the patients who were there.
sentences.zh: 那里的病人。

sentences.en: taking advantage of the fact that you couldn't see anyone in there.
sentences.zh: 利用那里看不见任何人的事实。

sentences.en: So one thing that the doctor said was most difficult about this was there was no information on what was going on or when this was going to be over.
sentences.zh: 所以医生说最困难的一点是，没有任何关于发生了什么或何时结束的信息。

sentences.en: finally the government did come out and say it was an act of sabotage that caused this.
sentences.zh: 最终政府确实出来说，这是一起破坏行为导致的。

sentences.en: Blaming the U.S.
sentences.zh: 指责美国

sentences.en: and the opposition for what had happened.
